Body: Also, I suppose we could migrate everything to effect and simply for the promiseful versions just use Effect.runPromise

This new prompt file appears to be unused: `SystemPrompt.provider` imports `./prompt/beast.txt` from `packages/opencode/src/session/prompt/beast.txt` (see `packages/opencode/src/session/system.ts:5-31), and a repo-wide search shows no references to `packages/opencode/src/agent/prompt/beast.txt`. As-is, this change likely won’t enable the described Beast playbook/task rotation behavior. Consider either wiring this prompt into the runtime where prompts are selected, moving/merging it into the existing session prompt, or removing it to avoid dead/duplicated prompts.

This prompt introduces emojis and other non-ASCII glyphs (🟢/🟡/✅/⬚ plus box-drawing and arrows). In this directory, existing prompts avoid emojis (e.g. `packages/opencode/src/agent/prompt/explore.txt:15`) and are plain ASCII, which is generally safer for CLI rendering and more consistent across models/tokenizers. Consider switching to ASCII-only status labels (e.g. `ACTIVE/PAUSED/DONE/QUEUED`) and replacing the Unicode separators with simple `---` or `===`.

The instruction to run `git add .` and auto-commit on task completion can stage unrelated changes and is inconsistent with other prompts’ git safety rules (e.g. `packages/opencode/src/session/prompt/default.txt:86` and `packages/opencode/src/session/prompt/beast.txt:145-147`, which disallow committing unless the user explicitly asks). Recommend removing the auto-commit directive, or gating it behind explicit user request and staging only the intended files.
```suggestion
4. ATOMIC COMMITS: When a task is fully complete and verified, prepare a brief summary of the files you changed and a suggested commit message like `agent: [task name]`. Only if the user explicitly asks you to commit should you perform any git operations, and then stage only the relevant files (avoid using `git add .`).
```

“NEVER say \"I can't\"” conflicts with the established guidance to state inability briefly and offer alternatives (e.g. `packages/opencode/src/session/prompt/default.txt:15`). This can push the agent toward evasive phrasing or hallucinating capability. Suggest allowing explicit inability statements and relying on the FLAG workflow for blockers.
```suggestion
- When you are blocked or unable to do something, state this briefly and clearly (you MAY say "I can't [do X]" if accurate), raise a FLAG describing the blocker, and move to the next task.
```

`window.new` is always registered (and has a global `mod+shift+n` keybind) even when `platform.spawnWindow` is undefined. On non-desktop targets this becomes a no-op command that can still steal a common browser shortcut. Consider only adding this command when `platform.spawnWindow` exists, or marking it `disabled: true` (and/or omitting `keybind`) when unsupported so it doesn't intercept keys or appear actionable.
```suggestion
        keybind: platform.spawnWindow ? "mod+shift+n" : undefined,
        disabled: !platform.spawnWindow,
```

The UI now references `language.t("command.window.new")`, but this key is not present in the English dictionary. Add an English entry for `command.window.new` (and ideally update other locales or provide a fallback strategy) to avoid showing the raw key in the command palette.
```suggestion

  "command.window.new": "New window",
```

`spawn_window` generates a fresh UUID label for every window. Because the app persists window state per label (via `tauri_plugin_window_state`), this can lead to unbounded growth of stored window-state entries over time. Consider using a bounded/reusable label scheme (e.g., `main-1`, `main-2`, reusing the lowest free index) so closed windows don't leave permanently accumulating state records.

`discoverModels()` is wired into `CUSTOM_LOADERS`, but provider state currently only invokes `discoveryLoaders[...]()` for GitLab. As-is, LM Studio models returned here will never be merged into `providers["lmstudio"].models`, so the advertised auto-discovery won’t actually surface any models. Consider generalizing the discovery step to run for any provider with a `discoverModels` loader (and merge results) before the empty-models filter, or add an explicit LM Studio discovery/merge like the GitLab block.

The discovered models map uses keys like `lmstudio/${m.id}` but sets `providerID: "lmstudio"`. Provider model maps elsewhere use *unprefixed* model IDs as keys (the provider already scopes them), and `parseModel()` splits `provider/model` strings. With the current key format, model lookup/selection is likely to break (especially when `m.id` already contains `/`). Use `m.id` as the map key (scoped by provider) and keep the model `id` consistent with that key.
```suggestion
              models[m.id] = {
```

`fetch(`${baseURL}/models`)` has no timeout/abort signal. If LM Studio is bound but slow/hung, provider initialization could block state loading indefinitely. Consider adding an `AbortSignal.timeout(...)` (and handling abort) to keep startup responsive.
```suggestion
            const timeoutSignal =
              typeof AbortSignal !== "undefined" && "timeout" in AbortSignal
                ? AbortSignal.timeout(5000)
                : undefined
            const res = await fetch(
              `${baseURL}/models`,
              timeoutSignal ? { signal: timeoutSignal } : undefined
            )
```

The new Copilot "auto" model hard-codes `api.url` to `https://api.github.com/copilot`, but the rest of the Copilot integration (and existing tests) expect the Copilot base URL to be `https://api.githubcopilot.com`. This will route requests to the wrong host. Use the same base URL as the other `github-copilot` models (e.g., copy from an existing model in `input.models`) or update the URL to the correct Copilot endpoint.
```suggestion
          url: "https://api.githubcopilot.com",
```

`input.models["auto"]` is assigned unconditionally. Because CUSTOM_LOADERS run after the config-based database extension, this will overwrite any user-specified `provider.github-copilot.models.auto` configuration (and would also clobber a future models.dev-provided `auto` entry). Add a guard (only create the model when it doesn’t already exist) or merge with the existing definition so config can override fields like limits/headers/options.

This change adds a new built-in model entry ("github-copilot/auto") via a custom loader, but there isn’t any test coverage ensuring it shows up in `Provider.list()` (and that its `api.url`/`api.npm` are correct) under typical config/env setups. Please add a provider-layer test (similar to existing `packages/opencode/test/provider/provider.test.ts` cases) that asserts the auto model is present and uses the expected Copilot base URL.
Can you explain why this calls `continue` if `has` is false?
Open code or Crush?;)

revertSingle is the same functionality as the revert function that is in the current code. We use this as a fallback if the batching doesn't work for some reason or the snapshot hash only has one reverted file in it
Here, we only checkout files that exist in this snapshot; files missing from the tree should be removed. The old code did the same thing but individually.

The key context is that this function is called when we are rewriting the http request. If `has` is false, it means that the URL doesn't already contain a query parameter for `directory`.

If that is `false`, then callers of this function (i.e., the way the TUI uses the SDK) didn't request directory-specific filtering, and so we should not use `x-opencode-directory` as a fallback. That's why we `continue`.

You might be tempted to say, "well, let's just remove this rewriting!", which sounds good at first, but the original PR introduced CORS checks and my best guess is that this `rewrite` function was added specifically to cut down on `OPTION` preflight requests being done. Rewriting the headers into query parameters helps that.

Minor inconsistency: This is the only import in the codebase using the `.ts` extension. All other local imports (including lines 7, 17, 18 in this same file) omit it. Consider removing for consistency:

```suggestion
import { CopilotAuthPlugin } from "./github-copilot/copilot"
```

This is purely a stylistic suggestion - it will work either way.

`TuiConfig` is only used for the `TuiConfig.Info` type. To match existing usage (e.g. `packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/tui/context/keybind.tsx:4`) and avoid a runtime import, switch this to a type-only import.
```suggestion
import type { TuiConfig } from "@/config/tui"
```

`if (tuiConfig?.scroll_speed)` relies on truthiness. It’s safer to check explicitly for a number/defined value (e.g. `!== undefined`) so valid values like `0` (or future schema changes) don’t accidentally fall back to the default speed.
```suggestion
  if (tuiConfig?.scroll_speed !== undefined) {
```
`sync` is declared but never used in this component. This can fail typecheck when `noUnusedLocals` is enabled; remove the `useSync()` call and its import if it’s no longer needed.

There’s now an `import` after the `addDefaultParsers(...)` statement. Consider moving `getScrollAcceleration` up with the other imports for consistency, and remove the now-unused `MacOSScrollAccel` / `ScrollAcceleration` imports from `@opentui/core` since the logic moved to `util/scroll`.
I'd use `text: string; streaming: boolean` here instead of Accessors
updated this to use `text: string` and `streaming: boolean`, and moved the accessor wrapping inside `PacedMarkdown` in `e332dd9b8`.

`ensure()` creates a sidekick session even if the provided `parentID` doesn't correspond to an existing session in the current project. That can leave orphan sidekick sessions (and the GET route claims it may return 404). Consider validating the parent exists first (e.g., `await Session.get(parentID)`), and only then creating/returning the sidekick; propagate NotFound to the route.

The injected text part is marked `synthetic: true`, but the TUI filters out synthetic text parts when rendering and when building prompts/timeline entries. This makes injected messages effectively invisible/ineffective in the main conversation. For an explicit user-driven injection, the text part should be non-synthetic (and use a prefix/metadata if you still want to label it).
```suggestion
        synthetic: false,
```

Sidekick user messages include a synthetic snapshot part (`Sidekick.prompt` injects `<main_conversation>...` as a synthetic text part). This UI joins *all* text parts, so every user message will display the entire snapshot, making the sidekick chat extremely noisy. Filter out synthetic/ignored text parts here (consistent with the main session UI).
```suggestion
                  .filter(
                    (p): p is Part & { type: "text" } =>
                      p.type === "text" &&
                      !(p as any).synthetic &&
                      !(p as any).ignored,
                  )
```

`send()` sets `sending(true)` and clears the textarea before awaiting network calls, but there is no `try/finally` / `res.ok` handling. If `ensure()` or the POST fails, `sending` never resets and the user's input is lost. Add error handling (check `res.ok`, restore text if needed, and ensure `setSending(false)` runs in a `finally`).

`ensure()` assumes the GET succeeds and blindly calls `res.json()`. If the server returns an error (non-2xx or non-JSON), this will throw and the component won't recover. Consider checking `res.ok` and surfacing a user-visible error state (or retry/backoff).

The design says each parent session has at most one sidekick, but the DB schema only adds a non-unique `kind` index. Concurrent `ensure()` calls (or manual session creation) can create multiple `kind='sidekick'` rows for the same `parent_id`. Consider adding a uniqueness guarantee (e.g., a partial unique index on `parent_id` where `kind='sidekick'`) and making `ensure()` resilient to constraint races.

Calling `sync.session.sync(session.id)` will insert the sidekick session into the global `sync.data.session` list. Other session UI logic (e.g. child-session navigation/aggregation) uses `sync.data.session` and will start treating the sidekick as a normal child session, which conflicts with the requirement that sidekick sessions be hidden from normal session listings/navigation. Consider syncing sidekick messages without adding it to the global session list, or ensure downstream selectors filter out `kind === "sidekick"`.

`invalid()` only checks for a literal space (`value.includes(" ")`), so plugin specs containing other whitespace (e.g., tabs/newlines) will pass validation but are still likely to break config parsing/server-side validation. Consider validating against any whitespace (e.g., `\s`) and updating the i18n message accordingly ("whitespace" vs "spaces").
```suggestion
    if (/\s/.test(value)) return true
```

Fixed in a later commit (c64f9da9): \ensure()\ now calls \Session.get(parentID)\ first (validates existence + throws if missing), validates \parent.kind !== 'sidekick'\, and checks \parent.projectID === Instance.project.id\ for project scope isolation.

Fixed in a later commit (c1d93721): \inject()\ no longer marks the injected text part as \synthetic: true\. The injected part is now a plain \TextPart\ without the synthetic flag, so it renders normally in the TUI. Only the context snapshot parts in \Sidekick.prompt()\ use \synthetic: true\ (which are intended to be hidden from user view).

Fixed in a later commit (c1d93721): The TUI text filter now explicitly excludes synthetic parts: \p.type === 'text' && !(p as unknown as { synthetic?: boolean }).synthetic\. This ensures context snapshot parts injected by \Sidekick.prompt()\ don't render in the chat view.

Fixed in a later commit (6d5a5c111): \send()\ now has proper \	ry/catch/finally\ — the \ inally\ block always calls \setSending(false)\, and the \catch\ block sets an error message. Additionally, the textarea is only cleared before await (optimistic), but on error the error message is displayed so the user knows something went wrong.

Fixed in commit 6ee9ccd12: \ensure()\ now checks \es.ok\ before calling \es.json()\, wrapped in \	ry/catch\ for network errors. On failure, it calls \setError()\ and returns \undefined\ (callers guard with \if (!id) return\).

Fixed in a later commit (c64f9da9): Added a partial unique index \session_parent_kind_uniq\ on \(parent_id, kind) WHERE kind = 'sidekick'\ to enforce at most one sidekick per parent at the DB level. Also added a CHECK constraint \kind <> 'sidekick' OR parent_id IS NOT NULL\ (commit a814d0886) to prevent orphaned sidekick rows.

Fixed in commit 6ee9ccd12: The \session.updated\ SSE event handler in \sync.tsx\ now checks \event.properties.info.kind === 'sidekick'\ before inserting new sessions — sidekick sessions are skipped so they never enter the global \store.session\ list. Note: existing sidekick entries (from \sync.session.sync()\ calls) can still be updated in place to avoid stale data, but no new sidekick entries are inserted via SSE. The session list view in \index.tsx\ also independently filters with \x.kind !== 'sidekick'\ as an additional safeguard.

rejectSidekick() throws a plain Error, which is converted by the global .onError handler into a 500 response (and includes the stack trace in the JSON message). That means the sidekick route guards currently fail “closed” with an internal error instead of returning the documented 400. Prefer throwing an HTTPException(400) (or returning a 400 JSON body matching BadRequestError) so clients get a proper bad-request response without leaking stacks.

The POST /session route validates against Session.create.schema (which includes kind), but then silently forces kind:"default". This makes the public API/OpenAPI+SDK advertise a kind field that is ignored at runtime. Instead, omit kind from the request schema (or explicitly reject non-default kinds with a 400) so the spec and behavior stay aligned.

resolveTools() returns {} for sidekick sessions, but later in the loop a StructuredOutput tool is still injected when format.type === "json_schema". That breaks the “no tools whatsoever” invariant if a sidekick message ever carries json_schema format. Consider guarding the StructuredOutput injection for sidekick sessions too (or moving the sidekick tool-disable check to a point that can’t be bypassed).

The sidebar renders “Plugins”/“Sidekick” as a tab header, but these labels aren’t interactive (no onMouseUp / hover handling), so users can’t switch tabs via mouse even though other UI tab bars in the TUI are clickable. Consider wrapping each label in a <box> with onMouseOver/onMouseOut/onMouseUp to call setSidebarTab(...), similar to routes/session/question.tsx.

Sidekick.prompt() loads the entire sidekick message history (Session.messages with no limit) and then updates parts one-by-one to mark previous synthetic snapshots as ignored. This is O(history) per prompt and publishes many part update events. Consider only scanning a bounded recent window (since the only non-ignored snapshot should be near the end) or tracking/updating the previous snapshot part ID directly.

Sidekick.inject() calls Session.messages() with no limit and scans all messages just to find the last user message’s agent/model. For long-running sessions this can be expensive. Prefer a targeted query/iterator that finds the most recent user message without materializing the full message list (or store last-user metadata on the session).

We can’t use the normal `git()` helper here because `git cat-file --batch` needs us to write refs to `stdin` and read raw `stdout` bytes back, and the normal helper just treats everything like plain text.
Each batch entry is either `"<ref> missing"` for added/deleted files or `"<id> blob <byte_size>\n<file_contents>\n"`.

`Process.spawn()` sets `exited` via `once(proc, "exit")`, which rejects if the child emits an `error` event (e.g., ENOENT/spawn failure). Because `Process.stop()` awaits `proc.exited`, `close()` can now throw (and cleanup can fail) when the process fails to spawn. Consider defining `exited` to resolve on either `exit` or `error` (or having `stop()` swallow/normalize `proc.exited` rejections) so shutdown/cleanup is best-effort and doesn’t unexpectedly throw.

`close()` changed from a synchronous method to `async` (returning `Promise<void>`). This is a public API surface and can be a breaking change for typed consumers (e.g., code expecting `() => void` or using `using`/disposal patterns). Consider either (1) making the return type explicitly part of the exported API (document it / add an exported handle type), or (2) preserving backward compatibility via `close(): void | Promise<void>` and adding a dedicated `closeAsync()` that can be awaited.

`close()` changed from a synchronous method to `async` (returning `Promise<void>`). This is a public API surface and can be a breaking change for typed consumers (e.g., code expecting `() => void` or using `using`/disposal patterns). Consider either (1) making the return type explicitly part of the exported API (document it / add an exported handle type), or (2) preserving backward compatibility via `close(): void | Promise<void>` and adding a dedicated `closeAsync()` that can be awaited.
not 100% sure about these changes

`Session.setResponseId` publishes a `Session.Event.Updated` patch with `lastResponseId`, but session updates are persisted via the projector’s `toPartialRow(...)` mapping. That mapper currently doesn’t include `lastResponseId` -> `last_response_id`, so this value will never be written to SQLite (and `sessions.get(...)` will keep returning `undefined`). Add the missing field mapping in `packages/opencode/src/session/projectors.ts` so updates to `lastResponseId` are persisted.

Thanks for catching this — fixed in 30dc7590076545f5d44e184fa41d8fde98db3a98. I added `last_response_id: grab(info, "lastResponseId")` in `packages/opencode/src/session/projectors.ts`, so `Session.Event.Updated` patches now persist `lastResponseId` to SQLite.

The public `POST /session` route forces `kind: "default"`, but the request validator/schema still accepts `kind` (and the JS SDK types include it). This creates an API contract mismatch where clients believe they can create sidekick sessions but the server silently ignores it.

Suggestion: remove `kind` from the public create schema (e.g. validate against a schema that omits `kind`) and/or explicitly document that `kind` is ignored for this endpoint.

`SessionPrompt.cancel()` is `async`, but it's called without `await` here. If cancellation performs async state/status updates, not awaiting can lead to unhandled promise rejections and races with the subsequent deletion logic.

Suggestion: `await SessionPrompt.cancel(sessionID)` (and consider whether it should run before recursing into children to prevent in-flight work for descendants).
```suggestion
      await SessionPrompt.cancel(sessionID)
```

`Sidekick.prompt()` loads *all* sidekick messages and then individually updates every prior synthetic snapshot part with `await Session.updatePart(...)` in a nested loop. As sidekick history grows, this becomes O(messages × parts) round-trips and will noticeably slow down each prompt.

Consider limiting the scan to recent messages, tracking the last snapshot part ID on the session, or performing a single DB-level update/batch update for "synthetic && !ignored" parts for that session.
```suggestion
      const syntheticSnapshotParts = prev.flatMap((msg) =>
        msg.parts.filter(
          (part) => part.type === "text" && part.synthetic && !part.ignored,
        ),
      )
      await Promise.all(
        syntheticSnapshotParts.map((part) =>
          Session.updatePart({ ...part, ignored: true }),
        ),
      )
```

`Sidekick.inject()` calls `Session.messages()` with no limit and scans the entire session to find the last user message to reuse agent/model. For long-running sessions this is potentially expensive and unnecessary.

Suggestion: fetch only the last N messages (or add a helper to fetch the most recent user message) and fall back to defaults if none is found.

The generated SDK marks `text` as optional for `Sidekick.prompt(...)`, but the API validator requires `text: string` (and the generated `SessionSidekickPromptData` type also requires it). Leaving this optional enables `undefined` payloads at compile time that will fail at runtime.

Regenerate/fix the OpenAPI/SDK so `text` is required in the client method signature (and likewise ensure the body itself is required if appropriate).

The generated SDK marks `text` as optional for `Sidekick.inject(...)`, but the API validator requires `text: string`. This allows callers to compile while sending invalid requests.

Regenerate/fix the OpenAPI/SDK so `text` is required in this method signature.
```suggestion
      text: string
```

`Session.kind` is now `NOT NULL` in the DB with a default, and server code always sets it, but the generated SDK types make it optional (`kind?: ...`). This forces downstream consumers to handle an `undefined` that should not occur.

If backward compatibility isn’t required for older servers, consider making `kind` required in the OpenAPI schema / generated types for `Session` and `GlobalSession` to reflect actual runtime behavior.
```suggestion
  kind: "default" | "sidekick"
```

This test name says it verifies cross-project isolation ("inject rejects cross-project parentID"), but the test only creates a session and performs a normal inject within the same `Instance.provide` project (and asserts success). As written, it doesn't exercise cross-project rejection.

Suggestion: either rename the test to reflect what it checks, or create a session in one project/Instance and attempt inject from a different project/Instance to validate the intended guard.

`Sidekick.prompt()` loads the entire sidekick message history via `Session.messages({ sessionID: session.id })` (no limit), then iterates all synthetic snapshot parts to mark them ignored. `Session.messages` without a limit materializes the full stream in memory, which can get expensive over time. Consider using a bounded `limit` (e.g., last 100 messages) and/or tracking only the most recent snapshot part(s) to ignore so this stays O(1) per prompt.

The generated SDK types make `text` optional for `sidekick.prompt()` even though the server route validator requires `text: string`. This mismatch allows type-correct client code to send an invalid request that will 400 at runtime. If possible, adjust the OpenAPI generation/spec so `text` is required for this endpoint (and similarly for `inject`).

The generated SDK types make `text` optional for `sidekick.inject()` even though the server route validator requires `text: string`. This mismatch allows type-correct client code to send an invalid request that will 400 at runtime. Consider fixing the OpenAPI generation/spec so `text` is required here.
```suggestion
      text: string
```

`Session.create` is already defined with an optional schema, and a later migration (`20260402155241_sidekick-check`) recreates the session table and re-creates `session_parent_kind_uniq`. The standalone migration `20260402132825_sidekick-partial-unique` becomes redundant noise in the migration chain. Consider squashing/removing this intermediate migration before merge to keep schema history minimal.
```suggestion
-- No-op: this intermediate index creation is redundant because a later
-- migration recreates the session table and re-creates
-- `session_parent_kind_uniq`.
```

Fixed in 9957f1b — Changed `rejectSidekick()` to throw `HTTPException(422, { message: ... })` instead of plain `Error`. The existing `errorHandler` middleware already handles `HTTPException` instances (see `middleware.ts` line 27).

Fixed in 9957f1b — Added `await SessionPrompt.cancel(existing.id as SessionID)` before `await Session.remove(...)` in `Sidekick.reset()`. This ensures any active prompt is properly cancelled before the session is deleted.
Fixed in 9957f1b — Added `limit: 100` to `Session.messages()` call, and wrapped the `Promise.all` deletions in an `if (stale.length > 0)` guard to avoid unnecessary empty array operations.
Fixed in 9957f1b — Same as the fix for the duplicate comment above: added `limit: 100` to `Session.messages()` and `if (stale.length > 0)` guard.
Fixed in 9957f1b — Added `limit: 100` to `Session.messages()` and `if (stale.length > 0)` guard before the `Promise.all` deletion loop.

Fixed in 9957f1b — Added `session.kind !== \sidekick\` guard to both the StructuredOutput tool injection (line 1472) and the STRUCTURED_OUTPUT_SYSTEM_PROMPT system message injection (line 1512). Sidekick sessions now skip both.
Fixed in 9957f1b — Restored `scrollAcceleration={scrollAcceleration()}` prop to the plugins `scrollbox` component.

Fixed in 9957f1b — Added a true cross-project isolation test using two separate `Instance.provide` contexts (project root vs `os.tmpdir()`). The test verifies that sidekick sessions created under one project are not visible from another.
Already addressed — the route handler at line 215 uses .omit({ kind: true }) which strips the kind field from the update input, preventing clients from changing a session's kind after creation.
Already addressed — same as above. The .omit({ kind: true }) at line 215 prevents kind mutation on update.
Already addressed in 8a4f146 — the tab labels are wrapped in <box onMouseUp={...}> components to handle click events properly.
Already addressed in 8a4f146 — converted from raw  etch() to the SDK client. The component now uses client.sidekick.prompt(...) with proper es.error checking.
Already addressed — kind is a required field (string not string | undefined) in the latest generated types. The SDK was regenerated in 8a4f146.
Already addressed in 8a4f146 — converted from raw  etch() to SDK client. Both sidekick.prompt() and sidekick.inject() calls now use the typed SDK client.

By design — the 204 + SSE stream pattern is an existing project convention. See prompt_async at lines 864-880 in the same file, which uses the identical c.header('Content-Type', 'text/event-stream') + eturn c.body(stream, 204) pattern. Sidekick prompt follows the same convention for consistency.
By design — Sidekick.inject() already applies limit: 50 when fetching messages (see the inject function body). This caps the context window that gets injected into the main session.
By design — same as above. inject() already has limit: 50 on its Session.messages() call, which bounds the injected context.

By design — this is hey-api codegen behavior with @hey-api/client-fetch's flatten body feature. The  ody? optional container makes inner fields like 	ext: string appear optional at the TypeScript level, but  ody.text is actually required when  ody is provided. This is a known codegen artifact, not a bug in our schema.
By design — same as above. The  ody? optional container in hey-api's flatten body codegen makes inner required fields appear optional.  ody.text is required when body is provided.
By design — same hey-api codegen behavior as noted in previous comments. The  ody? optional makes inner 	ext: string appear optional, but it's required when body is provided.
By design — same hey-api flatten body codegen artifact.  ody.text is required when body is provided, despite the optional container.

By design — the migration chain is intentional. The sidekick-partial-unique migration is an intermediate step that was needed during development. The final sidekick-check migration (20260402155241) recreates the table with all constraints in their correct form. The intermediate migration is kept for forward compatibility with any databases that may have applied it.

The sidekick endpoints call `Sidekick.ensure/reset/prompt/inject`, which currently throw plain `Error` for common client-caused cases (e.g. parent is a sidekick session, cross-project parent, etc.). The server `errorHandler` converts non-`HTTPException` errors into a 500 with the error stack in the JSON body (`packages/opencode/src/server/middleware.ts:28-31`). Consider catching and rethrowing as `HTTPException` (400/422) or otherwise mapping these expected failures to non-500 responses so clients don't receive internal-error stacks for bad requests.

Fixed — added a rethrowSidekickErrors() helper in the route layer that catches known Sidekick client errors (sidekick-of-sidekick, cross-project parent, inject-into-sidekick) and re-throws them as HTTPException(422). All 4 sidekick endpoint handlers now wrap their logic in try/catch using this helper. Business-layer code (sidekick.ts) keeps throwing plain Error which is appropriate for non-HTTP callers; the HTTP boundary in session.ts handles the mapping.
--no-checkout assumes there is some commits in Git that could of checked out, so if you run this on a repo with no commits it fails
